data.title: Abacavir + Lamivudine
data.summary: IV Antivirals — Antiretroviral (ART) · Fixed-dose combination of two NRTIs (nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors)
data.body:
_Oral · IV Antivirals — Antiretroviral (ART)_

**Class:** Fixed-dose combination of two NRTIs (nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors)

## Mechanism of action
- Both are nucleoside analogues, phosphorylated inside cells to active triphosphates
- They compete with natural nucleotides for HIV reverse transcriptase and cause chain termination of viral DNA
- Abacavir is a guanosine analogue (active form carbovir triphosphate); lamivudine is a cytidine analogue that is also active against hepatitis B

## Pharmacokinetics
- Both are well absorbed with or without food
- Abacavir: metabolised by alcohol dehydrogenase and glucuronidation (no CYP); lamivudine: excreted by the kidneys
- Long intracellular half-lives allow once-daily dosing

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Backbone of first-line ART in children (with dolutegravir) under the national (NACO) programme
- Adults when tenofovir cannot be used (e.g. renal disease, osteoporosis)

## Dose & formulations
- Adults: abacavir 600 mg + lamivudine 300 mg once daily
- Children: weight-band dosing with dispersible tablets (abacavir 120 mg + lamivudine 60 mg) as per NACO tables

## Adverse effects
- Abacavir hypersensitivity syndrome (about 5–8%, usually in the first 6 weeks): fever, rash, GI symptoms, malaise, cough or breathlessness
- It is strongly linked to HLA-B*57:01. Rechallenge after a reaction can be fatal, so never restart
- Abacavir: possible increase in myocardial infarction risk
- Lamivudine: very well tolerated; pancreatitis in children; flare of hepatitis B when stopped
- NRTI class: lactic acidosis and hepatic steatosis (rare with these two)

## Contraindications
- HLA-B*57:01 positive (test before use where available)
- Previous abacavir hypersensitivity (lifelong contraindication)
- Moderate–severe liver impairment (abacavir)

## Drug interactions
- Alcohol raises abacavir levels
- Lamivudine: co-trimoxazole raises levels slightly; do not combine with emtricitabine (same drug class and target)

## Monitoring
- CD4 count and viral load as per programme schedule
- Hepatitis B status before starting (lamivudine stopping can cause a flare)
- LFT; lipids; cardiovascular risk

## Pregnancy & lactation
Both can be used in pregnancy; the national programme prefers TLD (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir) for pregnant women.

## Viva points
- Abacavir hypersensitivity = HLA-B*57:01 — never rechallenge
- Lamivudine also treats hepatitis B; stopping it can cause a hepatitis flare
- Current NACO preferred first-line for adults is TLD; ABC + 3TC + DTG is used in children

## Note on sources
Wolverton covers ART only briefly (HLA associations and a list of drugs), so Khopkar and NACO were the main guides here. Regimens change often — please confirm with the latest NACO guidelines.

_Sources: Khopkar ch.4 (Antiretroviral drugs); Wolverton 4e ch.3 (HLA-B*57:01 pharmacogenetics) and ch.11; check against current NACO guidelines. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
